current_active_lexical_decision.rationale: The participle literally suggests being brought in/brought back. In this restoration context, and with the parallel exile language, 'who had returned' communicates the intended sense in idiomatic English without implying they returned entirely by their own initiative. 'Who had been brought back' is a viable more formal alternative.

current_reader_notes.text: Or, more literally, 'who had been brought back' from the captivity.
'From the captivity' means from the exile; compare the exile-restoration setting reflected in the Hebrew parallel.
